version.changelog:
1. **Fix chunk budget formula** — When mapping expands, budget reduction changes from 1:1 → ~0.49:1

2. **ContextOverflowError detection** — Detect prompt overflow + output truncation, preventing silent corruption

3. **Self-healing retry** — On overflow, automatically shrink chunk (×0.75) and retry up to 2 times

4. **Tool-Pair acceleration** — Skip Model-Pair, use diff algorithm to extract mapping, saving ~13.5% time

5. **16K fallback** — Default 8K, auto-upgrade to 16K only when mapping expansion causes insufficient budget

6. **Skill doc cleanup following "don't document what CLI owns" principle** — Removed 10 CLI internal details (pair strategy, server lifecycle, mapping path conventions, skip reason enums, etc.); added LLM prompting guidelines (the agent's core responsibility outside the CLI); fixed inconsistent tag format (`person_name` → `person name`)

7. **Unified batch output directory** — All batch default outputs moved from scattered user directories (`anonymized/`, `restored/`, `masked/`) into a unified `<input-dir>/.has/` hidden directory. Added `_default_restore_output_dir()` smart detection to ensure restore output is placed alongside `anonymized/` rather than nested inside `.has/`

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: has-anonymizer
Version: 1.0.2

The has-anonymizer skill bundle provides a legitimate and well-engineered toolset for on-device text and image anonymization. It demonstrates strong security practices, including restricting the inference server (llama-server) to local loopback addresses to ensure privacy, enforcing restrictive file permissions (0600) on sensitive mapping files in mapping.py and cli_utils.py, and implementing symlink escape protections in has_image.py and has_text/cli_utils.py. The logic is transparent, and the instructions in SKILL.md are strictly functional, aimed at guiding the agent to preserve privacy tags during interactions with cloud LLMs.

llm.summary: The skill's code, install steps, and runtime instructions are consistent with an on-device text/image anonymizer; it requests no unrelated credentials and only requires local model binaries and standard ML/image tooling.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (on-device text and image anonymization) aligns with the requested binaries (llama-server for text model inference, ultralytics/opencv/pillow for image processing) and the included code. The install spec downloads HaS text and image models from Hugging Face and installs uv/llama.cpp via brew (macOS), which matches the stated on-device model usage. Nothing gratuitous (no cloud API keys or unrelated credentials) is requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the CLI code limit actions to local anonymization workflows: scanning/hiding/restoring text, image detection and masking, starting a local llama-server on loopback, reading files in user-specified paths, and writing outputs/mappings. The code enforces safeguards (refuses to overwrite originals, checks for symlink escape, writes mapping files with restrictive permissions). It does start/monitor a local process and may call lsof/ps for inspection, which is appropriate for its server-management role.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Install uses brew formulas for uv and llama.cpp (macOS only) and downloads two large model files from huggingface.co (well-known host). Download installs are expected for model-based skills, but they do bring ~760 MB of artifacts to disk (two models). On non-macOS platforms, the provided install steps do not include brew alternatives for llama-server/uv, so installation will require manual setup.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No secrets or API keys are required. Optional environment variables (model paths, max parallel requests, verbose flags) are proportionate and documented. The skill does not request unrelated credentials or access to other skills' config.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled and uses normal agent invocation. It launches and may persist a local llama-server process while in use and writes logs to /tmp and model files to a models directory; this is consistent with its stated purpose and does not modify other skills or request elevated/system-wide changes.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be what it says: an on-device anonymizer for text and images that runs a local model server and image segmentation model. Before installing, consider: (1) disk space and bandwidth — the install downloads large model files (~760 MB total); (2) provenance — the models are fetched from Hugging Face; verify you trust the model owner and consider checking checksums or using your own vetted models; (3) platform support — the provided brew installs target macOS; on Linux/Windows you'll need to install llama-server/uv and Python dependencies manually; (4) runtime behavior — the skill will read files you point it at and may start a local llama-server bound to loopback (it refuses non-loopback hosts), and image masking is irreversible while text hiding can be restored via mapping files; (5) isolation — if you have sensitive assets, run the tool in a controlled environment until you are comfortable with results. No credentials are requested and there are no obvious exfiltration endpoints in the code.
